/-!
# Saturation of the shifted high-window relation system

The two-coordinate recurrence makes the pure windows
`S + q*S` normally generated by the multiplier window `S`.  Cofinal theta
exhaustion therefore realizes multiplication of a relation reading by every
coefficient of a pinned-chart ring at a later recursive relation stage.

The stage-one reading ideal is generated by relation readings.  Ideal-span
induction, with transport to a common later stage in the additive case, gives a
relation witness for every element of this ideal.  Subtracting such a witness
from an arbitrary section with the same reading reduces eventual saturation to
the high-window zero-read kernel-killing theorem.
-/

gives a simultaneous induction proving the fibre model and projectivity of
every finite-stage relation quotient over the nonreduced carve ring.
-/

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

     8	/-!
     9	# The widened classifier-clause endpoint
    10	
    11	`DivRepChartRangeAff` proves widened classifier surjectivity from a class on every carve chart
    12	whose classifier is the chart map.  A universal certified family naturally supplies the
    13	stronger characterizing clause `IsDivRepClassifyAff`, rather than that equality directly.
    14	This file is the small bridge between those interfaces; it does not duplicate the atlas
    15	factorization or away-span gluing.
    16	
    17	## Main declarations
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamilyAff.IsChartClause` -- every universal chart class
    20	  satisfies the widened classifier clause at the canonical chart map.
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepClassifyZarAff_surjective_of_chartClause` -- the clause implies
    22	  classifier surjectivity via the chart-range theorem.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause` -- the final widened
    24	  representability producer in the clause spelling.
    25	-/

    27	set_option autoImplicit false
    28	set_option quotPrecheck false
    29	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    30	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    33	
    34	open CategoryTheory
    35	
    36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    37	
    38	open Grassmannian Scheme

    49	  [IsIntegral C.left]
    50	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    51	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    52	  [IsDominant pi]
    53	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    54	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    55	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    56	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]

    70	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1

    73	local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
    74	  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)

    76	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

    80	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    81	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

    83	namespace DivRepChartFamilyAff

    85	/-- Every supplied widened chart class is classified by its canonical chart map. -/
    86	def IsChartClause

    88	      DivFamZarAff C (ChartRing i j) g) : Prop :=
    89	  ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),

   116	  fun v => exists_divRepClassifyZarAff_eq_of_chartRange

   119	
   120	include hO hchi in
   121	/-- Universal widened chart classes satisfying the characterizing clause represent the

   123	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause
   124	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   125	      DivFamZarAff C (ChartRing i j) g)
   126	    (hU : DivRepChartFamilyAff.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :
   127	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
   128	  divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartRange hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U
   129	    (divRepClassifyZarAff_left_eq_chartMap hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU)

   131	end Curve

     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam
    12	
    13	The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
    14	module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
    15	representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.
    16	
    17	The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
    18	two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
    19	representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.
    20	
    21	This is not an unconditional Picard representability result: the final declaration below retains
    22	both geometric inputs.  Moreover, at the larger admissible coverage parameter the raw Abel map has
    23	positive-dimensional linear-system fibres in positive genus, so the larger divisor representer
    24	cannot simply be substituted as an open chart source.  The remaining datum-tail construction is
    25	the corrected Altman--Kleiman step: represent the quotient by equality of the induced Picard class,
    26	thereby removing those fibres before applying the Picard representability seam.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
    31	  genus-parameter divisor representer.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
    34	  source opens.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` is the conditional final assembly
    36	  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
    37	-/
    38	
    39	set_option autoImplicit false
    40	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    41	
    42	universe u
    43	
    44	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    45	
    46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    47	
    48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    49	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    50	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    51	
    52	noncomputable section
    53	
    54	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
    55	def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    56	    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
    57	  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    58	
    59	/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
    60	corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
    61	theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    62	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    63	    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
    64	      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    65	  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    66	    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
    67	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    68	  exact h.symm
    69	
    70	/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
    71	representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
    72	def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    73	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    74	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    75	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    76	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    77	  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg
    78	
    79	/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
    80	morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
    81	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    82	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    83	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    84	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    85	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    86	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
    87	      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
    88	  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i
    89	
    90	/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
    91	Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
    92	unconditional divisor representer. -/
    93	def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    94	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    95	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    96	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    97	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    98	    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    99	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
   100	
   101	/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
   102	followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
   103	lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
   104	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   105	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   106	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   107	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   108	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
   109	      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   110	  calc
   111	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i =
   112	        chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart
   113	          (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)) i := rfl
   114	    _ = (V i).ι ≫ chartHom C
   115	          (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) i :=
   116	      chartHom_restrictChart
   117	        (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i
   118	    _ = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
   119	      congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·)
   120	        (chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i)
   121	
   122	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
   123	family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.
   124	
   125	The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
   126	`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
   127	Zariski local representability. -/

   131	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))

   133	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
   134	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
   135	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by

   137	      (Sigma.desc (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :=
   138	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ hcov
   139	  exact ⟨_, pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) hf⟩
   140
